articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals Related to North Korea and DRC

These actions aim to counter illicit activities supporting the North Korean regime and address destabilizing actions within the DRC.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking and Rejecting Transactions

These revisions aim to offer greater clarity and assistance to financial institutions and other entities in complying with OFAC regulations.
The updated FAQs are a resource for understanding compliance obligations and reporting requirements.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses for Iran and Russia
body: On October 21, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related designations, targeting a network of legal, maritime, and shipping service providers allegedly facilitating Iran's sanctions evasion and petroleum trade.

Concurrently, OFAC removed Belarusian national Andrei Alekseevich Rybakov from the Belarus sanctions list and Chinese national Lu Hezheng and two China-based animation studios from the North Korea sanctions list.

The agency also issued new Iran-related General Licenses GG and HH, authorizing certain wind-down activities through November 20, 2026, and Russia-related General License 131K, replacing and superseding GL 131J.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Designations and General Licenses Under Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations and associated General Licenses on October 19, 2026, under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA).
These actions aim to combat the theft of American intellectual property and protect U.S. economic interests.
The accompanying General Licenses are intended to mitigate unintended consequences and provide guidance for compliance.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and FAQ
body: On October 16, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and an updated Frequently Asked Question (FAQ).
This action modifies existing authorizations pertaining to Venezuela, reflecting ongoing policy adjustments.
The amendment and FAQ aim to provide clarity to stakeholders regarding permissible activities under the Venezuela sanctions program.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian and Cuban Entities, Issues New General Licenses
body: On October 15, 2026, OFAC imposed blocking sanctions against 16 individuals in Iran and the UAE and 10 entities—eight in Iran, one in Iraq, and one in Hong Kong—for their roles in Iran's international financial networks and shadow banking activities.
The action was taken under Executive Order 13902 as part of Operation Economic Outcast.

Additionally, OFAC issued General License FF, authorizing qualifying wind-down transactions involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance through October 30, 2026, and the State Department imposed blocking sanctions against Banco Internacional de Comercio, S.A. (BICSA), a Cuban state-owned bank, under Executive Order 14404.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuelan Individual from SDN List

This delisting is part of Washington's broader diplomatic recognition of the interim Venezuelan government.
The removal signifies a shift in U.S. policy towards certain Venezuelan officials.

articles.headline: DHS Updates Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List, Adding Three Entities
body: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), as Chair of the Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force (FLETF), announced an update to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List, effective October 29, 2026.

This update adds three entities to the list under UFLPA Section 2(d)(2)(B)(ii), which identifies entities working with the government of the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region to recruit, transport, transfer, harbor, or receive forced labor or members of persecuted groups out of Xinjiang.

The newly added entities are Baoding LYSZD Trade And Business Co., Ltd., Hetian Haolin Hair Accessories Co. Ltd. (and two aliases), and Hetian Taida Apparel Co., Ltd (and one alias), all listed under the category of entities in Xinjiang that mine, produce, or manufacture goods with forced labor.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
